entries.title: Proverbs 26:7
segments: 7. legs ... equal--or, "take away the legs," or "the legs ... are weak." In any case the idea is that they are the occasion of an awkwardness, such as the fool shows in using a parable or proverb (see (unresolved link);

entries.title: Proverbs 26:8
segments: 8. A stone, bound in a sling, is useless; so honor, conferred on a fool, is thrown away.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:9
segments: 9. As vexatious and unmanageable as a thorn in a drunkard's hand is a parable to a fool. He will be as apt to misuse is as to use it rightly.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:10
segments:
10. Various versions of this are proposed (Compare Margin). Better perhaps--"Much He injures (or literally, "wounds") all who reward," &c., that is, society is injured by encouraging evil men. 
 
    transgressors--may be rendered "vagrants." The word "God" is improperly supplied.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:11
segments: 11. returneth ... folly--Though disgusting to others, the fool delights in his folly.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:12
segments: 12. The self-conceited are taught with more difficulty than the stupid.
